name: Anserma
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Choco language of Colombia; only vocabulary lists (Rivet 1943) and 2011 rediscovery note (Rendon-Garcia); no phonology/stress description found.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page anse1238 and name search 'umbra'
sources.note: n/a; confirms 0 grammar/phonology/sketch references (4 refs: Rendón 2011 wordlist, Robledo 1539/1892, Rivet 1946), AES extinct, and no separate 'Umbra' languoid.

sources.citation: González, Simón. 2025. ¿Es el umbra una lengua chocó?: un primer acercamiento desde la lingüística comparada. Lengua y Sociedad 24(2): e27921. doi:10.15381/lengsoc.v24i2.27921 (34 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress: sections are conceptual framework, sources, Swadesh-list comparison and sound correspondences with Chocó languages; the only suprasegmental mention is 'i (con suprasegmentos)' / 'a (con suprasegmentos)' in Table 1 of Umbra-Embera Chamí correspondences.

sources.citation: González Ticora, Simón. 2021. Lengua Umbra como lengua chocó: una clasificación en disputa. Informe de investigación, Universidad de los Andes, Bogotá. 105 pp. (hdl 1992/60722)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement of stress placement anywhere (0 hits for acento/acentuación/penúltima/aguda etc.). Only the annex 'Conversión de símbolos vernáculos al AFI' decodes Rendón's (2011) suprasegmental notation: 'V́ -> *V́ (stress)', '̄V -> *V (entonación media)', 'V́V -> *Ṽ̂ (entonación descendente)', and 'ḿ -> *m silábica con stress', 'ŕ -> *ɾ silábica con stress', etc. -- i.e. Rendón marks stress lexically with an acute in his transcriptions; no rule is given.

sources.citation: Caicedo, Luis Javier. [2013]. La cuestión Umbra. 12 pp. (Personería de Riosucio / jenzera.org)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; ethnohistorical essay that summarises Rendón 2011's claims with page references (Chocó affiliation p.12-13, 'extensa variedad de sonidos' p.33, nasalization p.22) and reports that no audio recordings were kept from the 1995 investigation.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. & Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: CUP (section 2.6 on Chocó and the extinct Cauca-valley languages incl. Anserma)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100.A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l); the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.harvard_location: Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100 .A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l
sources.note: Authoritative statement of what is (not) known about Anserma; expected to confirm it is attested only by a few words, useful for closing the record rather than for a stress rule.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1943. Nouvelle contribution à l'étude de l'ethnographie précolombienne de Colombie. JSA 35: 25-39. doi:10.3406/jsa.1943.2342
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Compiles the entire colonial Anserma word corpus; would confirm that no accentual information exists for Anserma proper (expected silent).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (es) 'Idioma umbra'; Wikipedia (en) 'Anserma language' (extracts saved as JSON)
sources.note: Used for leads only. The Spanish article (sourced to Rendón 2011) gives transcriptions with acute accents on varying syllables, e.g. [daʧiíru], [xũxúɾãi], [taɾãbá], [ɐɾɐ̃nda], [ãʧú], but states no stress rule.

sources.citation: Ugarte Rico, A., Largo, M., Uribe, F. 2013. Historia de Guacuma. Pereira. (community volume containing the 'Umbra literario B' wordlist with its own accent/length conventions)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Second independent transcription source for Umbra ('Historia de Guacuma' conventions include V́ = stress, VV = length per González 2021); might comment on accent, though primarily a wordlist.

sources.citation: Rendón G., Guillermo. 2011. La lengua Umbra: Descubrimiento - Endolingüística - Arqueolingüística. Manizales: Zapata (Instituto de Altos Estudios). 287 pp. ISBN 978-958-57127-0-6
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only book-length description of the language filed under anse1238 (phonetics chapter around pp. 33-59 per Caicedo's page refs; uses an acute 'stress' diacritic throughout); if any first-hand statement on Umbra stress placement exists, it is here.

sources.citation: Aguirre García, Janner Johao. 2024. Nũkũrikumá. El pensamiento de los Ansermas: Análisis de la pragmática del lenguaje propio de la comunidad indígena Cartama.. Trabajo de grado, Universidad de Caldas (hdl ucaldas/21685)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: DSpace metadata/abstract only: a pragmatics/ethnographic thesis on the Cartama (Anserma-descendant) community whose abstract speaks of the 'exterminio irreparable de nuestra lengua propia'; not a phonological description, not downloaded.
